newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says may export more oil to aid producers.
newsitem.headline: Russia says may export more oil to aid producers.

text.p: Russia may export an additional 3.9 million tonnes (78,000 barrels per day) of oil a year over an unspecified time to raise cash to reduce producers' debts to the federal budget, Interfax news agency said on Tuesday.

It quoted Alfred Kokh, the privatisation minister, as saying he considered such a scheme, proposed by a company associated with oil giant LUKoil, "promising". The scheme would involve oil companies borrowing $1.5 billion abroad and issuing government-backed paper guaranteeing exports to the West.

It was not clear whether the proposal would increase Russia's total oil exports, which are running at about two million bpd, or displace shipments made under federal export programmes, which are state-mandated deliveries abroad.
Russia was producing at a rate of 5.83 million bpd over the first four months of this year.
Domestic oil, gas, electricity and coal companies owed the budget 29 trillion roubles ($5 billion) as of May. Of that total, about 34 oil and gas companies owe 100 billion ($17.4 million) roubles.
